newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Dao Heng in HK$1.2 bln launch.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Dao Heng in HK$1.2 bln launch.

text.p: Dao Heng Bank launched a HK$1.2 billion floating rate certificate of deposit issue into Asian debt markets Thursday, adding to an already ample supply of paper in the market.
The three-year certificates pay a margin of 36 basis points over the three-month Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate and, with fees, an all-in return of 43.5 basis points to top-tier participants.
China Development Finance Co (HK) and HSBC Markets are joint bookrunners.
Dao Heng is rated A3 by Moody's Investors Service.
Application has been made to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to accept the certificates as eligible for its Liquidity Adjustment Facility, or discount window.
Eligibility for LAF makes an issue more attractive to banks because holders of the qualifying debt can engage in repurchase agreements with the monetary authority, increasing liquidity.
At 43.5 basis points, Dao Heng's deal pays a fraction less than Bank of East Asia's three-year A3-rated FRCD transaction, which offers 44 basis points to the top tier.
Bankers said the pricing on the Dao Heng deal seems about right, but they pointed out that the market is flush with paper now and more is on the way.
"The market is starting to get a bit toppy," said one syndicate manager.
"Sooner or later it will be reflected in deals not being oversubscribed and then perhaps a litle in the pricing because people will have to start saying no," he said.

In addition to Bank of East Asia's HK$1.8 billion deal, Dah Sing Bank is in the market with a HK$1.2 billion issue and Bank of China Hong Kong branch recently completed it blockbuster HK$4 billion transaction.
And rumours were circulating that the Hong Kong branch of a major U.S. bank is eyeing a HK$1.5 billion LAF-eligible issue before year-end.
Spreads on LAF paper generally have narrowed this year because of plentiful liquidity in the Hong Kong banking sector.
In other news, Korea Development Bank launched its US$500 million seven-year global bond via Merrill Lynch and JP Morgan.
The bond will be priced during New York hours to yield 48-50 basis points over comparable Treasuries.
This is the first bond for a South Korean quasi-sovereign since the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) invited South Korea to join the group.
Korean bond yields already have come in sharply over the last year. KDB launched a US$500 million seven-year global one year ago that priced to yield 75 basis points over Treasuries.

In the local currency debt scene, Taiwan's central bank said it had approved the Asian Development Bank's application to issue Taiwan dollar-denominated bonds worth T$7 billion, or about US$255 million.
Chinatrust Bank is the lead underwriter of the issue, which is expected to have a term of seven or 10 years.
The ADB launched its first Taiwan-dollar denominated bond in August 1995.
Taiwan central bank and finance ministry officials have said that the ADB's bond issues would help internationalise Taiwan's bond market and raise the creditability of Taiwan's currency.
